airport: Airports show long, straight runways with distinct markings, connected to large terminal buildings, hangars, and aircraft parking stands. They differ from railway stations by having runways and terminals rather than train tracks and platforms; commercial areas show retail buildings rather than aviation infrastructure; bridges show crossing structures rather than airport facilities.
beach: Beaches appear as sandy or pebbly shorelines along water bodies, with light colors, wave patterns, and occasional beach umbrellas. They contrast with mountains by being coastal lowland rather than elevated rocky terrain; rivers show flowing water channels rather than sandy shores; deserts show inland sand dunes without water adjacency.
bridge: Bridges show elevated roadway or railway structures spanning over water or valleys, with visible pillars, deck, and approach ramps. They differ from rivers by being man-made crossing structures rather than water channels; viaducts span over land with multiple supports rather than water; ports show waterfront docks rather than crossing structures.
commercial: Commercial areas show dense retail and office buildings with large parking lots, wide streets, and visible storefronts. They contrast with parking lots by having buildings alongside vehicle storage; ports show water and docks rather than retail blocks; residential areas show housing units rather than commercial buildings.
desert: Deserts show vast, barren landscapes with sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse dry vegetation, with uniform light tones. They contrast with farmland by lacking crop rows and irrigation; beaches show coastal sandy areas adjacent to water; mountains show elevated rocky peaks rather than flat sand.
farmland: Farmland appears as large, open agricultural fields with uniform crop rows, regular field boundaries, and occasional irrigation. It differs from desert by having organized crops and vegetation rather than sand; meadow shows natural grassland without field lines; airports show runways and terminals rather than crop fields.
footballfield: Football fields show rectangular grassy areas with clear boundary lines, goal zones, and often surrounding tracks. They contrast with meadow by having sports markings and maintained grass rather than natural vegetation; parks have walking paths and trees rather than field markings; commercial areas show buildings rather than sports fields.
forest: Forests show dense tree canopy with dark green textures, irregular edges, and no visible ground, often covering large areas. They contrast with ponds by having dense vegetation rather than water features; mountains show exposed rock and elevation rather than tree cover; airports show runways rather than forest canopy.
industrial: Industrial areas feature large warehouses, factories, smokestacks, and extensive parking lots with regular blocky layouts. They differ from railway stations by having factories rather than passenger platforms and tracks; parking lots show vehicle storage without buildings; commercial areas show retail rather than industrial structures.
meadow: Meadows show open, grassy areas with smooth, uniform texture, often with scattered trees or shrubs, and no field lines. They contrast with farmland by lacking organized crop rows; football fields have sports markings rather than natural grass; parks have paths and recreational areas rather than open meadow.
mountain: Mountains show elevated, rugged terrain with steep slopes, rocky outcrops, and shadow patterns, often with forested lower elevations. They contrast with forests by having exposed rock and elevation changes rather than uniform tree cover; beaches show coastal sandy areas rather than mountainous terrain; rivers show water channels rather than rocky peaks.
park: Parks show green open spaces with trees, walking paths, ponds, and recreational areas, often irregular in shape. They differ from ponds by being larger areas with vegetation and paths rather than just water; commercial areas show buildings and parking rather than parkland; meadows show open grass without recreational paths.
parking: Parking lots appear as flat, paved areas with rows of vehicles, clear lane markings, and entrance points. They differ from commercial areas by having vehicle storage rather than buildings; viaducts show elevated road structures rather than ground-level parking; industrial areas have warehouses alongside parking rather than just open lots.
pond: Ponds appear as small, circular or irregular water bodies with calm surfaces, often surrounded by vegetation. They contrast with rivers by being still, enclosed water rather than flowing channels; parks are larger green areas with paths and trees rather than just water; forests show tree cover without water features.
port: Ports show waterfront areas with docks, piers, ships, cranes, and large storage areas adjacent to water. They differ from commercial areas by having ships and docks rather than retail buildings; residential areas show housing units rather than port infrastructure; bridges are crossing structures rather than waterfront facilities.
railwaystation: Railway stations show tracks, platforms, passenger buildings, and surrounding parking lots, often with linear rail lines. They contrast with industrial areas by having passenger platforms rather than factories; viaducts show elevated rail structures rather than ground-level stations; airports have runways rather than train tracks.
residential: Residential areas show housing units with visible roofs, yards, driveways, and street networks, with varied lot sizes. They differ from commercial areas by having housing rather than retail buildings; industrial areas show factories and storage rather than homes; ports show waterfront infrastructure rather than residential neighborhoods.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, sinuous, dark water channels with flowing patterns and riparian vegetation along banks. They contrast with ponds by being elongated flowing water rather than still water bodies; beaches show sandy shorelines along water rather than the water channels themselves; bridges are structures spanning across rivers.
viaduct: Viaducts show elevated road or rail structures with long continuous sections and multiple supports, often crossing over land. They differ from bridges by spanning over land rather than water; parking lots are ground-level open areas without elevated structures; railway stations are ground-level with tracks rather than elevated infrastructure.
